stated: Reform UK will scrap the remainder of the HS2 project, projecting a saving of £25 billion.

source.quote: Scrap HS2 Save £25 billion by scrapping the rest of this bloated vanity project.

bearing_set.reason: HS2 was designed partly to shift long-distance passengers from road and air to lower-emission rail; scrapping the remaining phase removes that capacity, plausibly worsening the UK's emissions trajectory.

Phase 1 of HS2 is actively under construction employing tens of thousands of workers in construction and supply chains; mid-project cancellation has a direct, non-negligible effect on employment and job security for those workers.

Cancelling a £25bn+ infrastructure commitment directly affects the debt path and fiscal headroom — a material shift in public-finance sustainability whichever way you judge whether the saving is redirected or absorbed.

HS2 was designed to raise inter-city rail capacity, ease congestion on the West Coast Main Line, and boost regional connectivity and productivity; scrapping the remainder removes those projected long-run living-standard and economic-opportunity gains, a concrete and significant mechanism.

membership_note: Three fundamentals earn a real verdict: fiscal sustainability (O12, the £25bn saving), long-run prosperity and connectivity (O13, loss of capacity/productivity gains), and environment (O6, rival modal-shift vs. construction-damage mechanisms). No bearing on O1/O2/O3/O4/O5/O7/O8/O9/O10/O11/O14/O15 — any effects there are indirect and negligible compared with these three.
